etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from French attaque, derived from the verb attaquer, from Italian attaccare (“to join, attach”) (used in attaccare battaglia (“to join battle”)), from Frankish *stakka (“stick”). Doublet of attach. Displaced native Old English on rǣsan (“to attack”) and onrǣs (“an attack”).

definitions.definition: (gaming) Any of several specific maneuvers, skills, or special abilities that a character can use to inflict damage against opponents.

quote.citation: 2002 March, Aaron Butler, “Mimesis Online (PC)”, in GameSpy.com‎[1], archived from the original on 2002-12-16:
quote.text: Combat in Mimesis Online is nice and simple. You click on your target  […]  and then keep right-clicking your chosen attack from the drop down menu. Every time you right click on the attack, your character will swing, shoot, etc.

quote.citation: 2022 January 28, Chris Tapsell, “Pokémon Legends Arceus Kleavor boss fight: How to beat Kleavor”, in Eurogamer.ner‎[2]:
quote.text: Kleavor has several attacks that it's worth roughly memorising: a charge attack, where it runs at you quickly; a jump attack, that causes a pillar of rock to spike out from under the ground; and a spin attack that does damage in a circle around it.

definitions.definition: An attempt to cause damage, injury to, or death of opponent or enemy.

quote.citation: 1983, Richard Ellis, The Book of Sharks, Knopf, →ISBN, page 161:
quote.text: From 1906 to 1960, there were forty-six recorded shark attacks, half of which were fatal.

quote.citation: 2013 July 19, Mark Tran, “Denied an education by war”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 6, page 1:
quote.text: One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on schools […] as children, teachers or school buildings become the targets of attacks. Parents fear sending their children to school. Girls are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence.

definitions.definition: An attempt to detract from the worth or credibility of, a person, position, idea, object, or thing, by physical, verbal, emotional, or other assault.

quote.citation: 1913, Robert Barr, chapter 4, in Lord Stranleigh Abroad‎[3]:
quote.text: “I came down like a wolf on the fold, didn’t I ?  Why didn’t I telephone ?  Strategy, my dear boy, strategy. This is a surprise attack, and I’d no wish that the garrison, forewarned, should escape. …”

definitions.definition: A time in which one attacks; the offence of a battle.
(informal, by extension) The beginning of active operations on anything.
(computing) An attempt to exploit a vulnerability in a computer system.
(cricket) Collectively, the bowlers of a cricket side.
(volleyball) Any contact with the ball other than a serve or block which sends the ball across the plane of the net.
(lacrosse) The three attackmen on the field or all the attackmen of a team.
(medicine) The sudden onset of a disease or condition.
An active episode of a chronic or recurrent disease.
(music) The onset of a musical note, particularly with respect to the strength (and duration) of that onset.

quote.citation: 2004, Gary Giddins, Weather Bird: Jazz at the Dawn of Its Second Century, page 322:
quote.text: Eric Reed was a curious choice as pianist, since his busy Petersonian attack is the antithesis of Lewis's, but he acquitted himself with panache,  […]

definitions.definition: (audio) The amount of time taken for the volume of an audio signal to go from zero to maximum level (e.g. an audio waveform representing a snare drum hit would feature a very fast attack, whereas that of a wave washing to shore would feature a slow attack).
(oenology) The initial sensory impact of a wine.
(transitive) To apply violent force to someone or something.

quote.citation: 1941 December 8, President Franklin D. Roosevelt, 0:00 from the start, in Day of Infamy Speech‎[4], Washington, D.C., page 1:
quote.text: Yesterday, December seventh, 1941, a date which will live in infamy, the United States of America was suddenly and deliberately attacked by naval and air forces of the Empire of Japan.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To aggressively challenge a person, idea, etc., with words (particularly in newspaper headlines, because it typesets into less space than "criticize" or similar).

quote.citation: 1988 December 11, John D'Emilio, “Enemies, Anger, and Militance”, in Gay Community News, volume 16, number 22, page 5:
quote.text: It was puzzling to read a column that claimed to be attacking me, yet espoused the main ideas in my article.

quote.citation: 2012 June 3, Nathan Rabin, “TV: Review: THE SIMPSONS (CLASSIC): “Mr. Plow” (season 4, episode 9; originally aired 11/19/1992)”, in The A.V. Club‎[5], Fusion Media Group:
quote.text: In its God-like prime, The Simpsons attacked well-worn satirical fodder from unexpected angles, finding fresh laughs in the hoariest of subjects.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To begin to affect; to act upon injuriously or destructively; to begin to decompose or waste.

quote.citation: 1849–1861, Thomas Babington Macaulay, chapter XXV, in The History of England from the Accession of James the Second, volume (please specify |volume=I to V), London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, →OCLC:
quote.text: On the fourth of March he was attacked by fever.

quote.citation: 1866, Balfour Stewart, An Elementary Treatise on Heat:

definitions.definition: (transitive) To deal with something in a direct way; to set to work upon.

quote.text: He filled a basin with water, and, with an old brush and piece of sandsoap, attacked the stove.

definitions.definition: (transitive, cricket) To aim balls at the batsman’s wicket.
(intransitive, cricket) To set a field, or bowl in a manner designed to get wickets.
(intransitive, cricket) To bat aggressively, so as to score runs quickly.
(soccer) To move forward in an active attempt to score a point, as opposed to trying not to concede.

quote.citation: 2011 October 15, Michael Da Silva, “Wigan 1 - 3 Bolton”, in BBC Sport‎[7]:
quote.text: Six successive defeats had left them rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table but, clearly under instructions to attack from the outset, Bolton started far the brighter.

definitions.definition: (cycling) To accelerate quickly in an attempt to get ahead of the other riders.
(physical chemistry) (Of a chemical species) To approach a chemical species or bond in order to form a bond with it.
Designed or kept for the purpose of confrontation.

pronunciation: Received Pronunciation, General American, General Australian
